items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: a man named Sullivan. Unfortunately, Sullivan was a North Irishman, a Protestant and a member of the Klan and they burned a cross in our yard a couple of weeks later.

ctx.x: Mississippi. And Catholics were not very popular, either. We were Catholics. And it wasn't too much of a problem with black people because there weren't that many black families in Tracy. But they took out their venom on the Mexicans, the Japanese farmers and the Catholic families.

My father worked on the railroad and he once found a list in one of the cabooses of members of the Ku Klux Klan and he turned it into the division headquarters thinking he would get the guys to lay off, a man named Sullivan. Unfortunately, Sullivan was a North Irishman, a Protestant and a member of the Klan and they burned a cross in our yard a couple of weeks later.
They burned a cross in your yard?
